title: MEME: Multi-Entity & Evolving Memory Evaluation
claim: Evaluation tasks can be organized along two axes, entity scope and temporal dynamics, so each quadrant exposes a distinct capability.
layout: 2x2 quadrant grid, central crossing axes, icon beside each quadrant title
description: A 2x2 grid of rounded, pastel-colored quadrants separated by a crossing pair of black arrows. The vertical axis runs from Static at the bottom to Evolving at the top. The horizontal axis runs from Single-entity on the left to Multi-entity on the right. Top-left, in yellow, is State Management, with a note-and-pencil icon and two bullets: Tracking (facts evolution history) and Deletion (explicit fact removal). Top-right, in red/pink, is Dependency Reasoning, with a tree-graph icon and two bullets: Cascade (updates propagate to dependent facts) and Absence (updates make dependent facts uncertain). Bottom-left, in blue, is Single-Fact Retrieval, with a magnifying glass and the bullet Exact Recall (verbatim reproduction). Bottom-right, in green, is Multi-Fact Retrieval, with a clipboard icon and the bullet Aggregation (combine multiple facts). Bold titles draw the eye first.
caption: MEME’s taxonomy of memory operations along two dimensions: entity scope (single vs. multi-entity) and temporal dynamics (static vs. evolving), with six tasks distributed across the four quadrants.
abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly operate in persistent environments where they must store, update, and reason over information across many sessions. While prior benchmarks evaluate only single-entity updates, MEME defines six tasks spanning the full space defined by the multi-entity and evolving axes, including three not scored by prior work: Cascade and Absence (dependency reasoning) and Deletion (post-removal state). Evaluating six memory systems spanning three memory paradigms on 100 controlled episodes, we find that all systems collapse on dependency reasoning under the default configuration (Cascade: 3%, Absence: 1% in average accuracy) despite adequate static retrieval performance. Prompt optimization, deeper retrieval, reduced filler noise, and most stronger LLMs fail to close this gap. The largest gain comes from a file-based agent paired with Claude Opus 4.7 as its internal LLM, which partially closes the gap at roughly 70x the baseline cost. Code and data are available on the project page: https://seokwonjung-jay.github.io/meme-eval/
